reviews.decision: Reaffirm the split between resolving a document-stated URI and opening it. Table 210/Base interpretation and IsMap geometry belong to document processing; handing Event::OpenUri to a host is not authority to fetch or invoke a handler.
reviews.evidence: pdf-model action URI parsing, viewer-core link/outline/OpenAction paths, viewer-host may_open_uri policy, and URI/Base tests. No network/external handler was invoked.

reviews.decision: Reaffirm the host's document-location fallback for a partial URI when no usable document Base resolved it. This follows Table 210/211 plus #256 scope but remains distinct from browser/network action.
reviews.evidence: viewer-host::policy::resolve_uri and host_mappings.rs tests use the opened document's location and preserve unresolved relative references when no location exists.

reviews.decision: Reaffirm link handling levels as host authorization policy. ISO's URI-resolution requirement does not require automatic external launch; current host policy can ask/refuse and no request should be generated by this audit.
reviews.evidence: viewer-host policy consumers receive OpenUri; host policy has explicit Links levels and defaults/controls recorded in the current host policy shard.

reviews.decision: The outline IsMap exception is directly source-stated and has a consumer path; the current corpus test establishes only URI handoff, not this explicit exception. A valid public regression should compare the same IsMap=true action reached through an outline item (bare URI) and annotation click (rounded coordinates). This is a test gap, not evidence of a current failure.
reviews.evidence: ADR 0144 cites Table 210 and routes outline activation through perform with no pointer position. Existing headless.rs test an_outline_item_whose_action_is_a_uri_hands_it_over does not set IsMap or assert the URI string. Proposed draft: drafts/uri_ismap_outline_spec_audit.rs.

reviews.decision: No new finding is claimed for common Next ordering. The earlier action_chains_current parent review records repeated-child and cycle execution; this pass reads Table 196 as context and retains its manual-interruption sentence as an unresolved bounded question because the current action walker silently bounds its list and no sequence cancellation mechanism was found.
reviews.evidence: action.rs MAX_ACTIONS/MAX_VISITS and Walk::push; viewer-core perform/resolve callers; no user cancellation handle is passed to this synchronous action walk. Note 1's interruption sentence is not literally implemented by the numeric cap. Whether broader host event-loop cancellation can satisfy it was not established.
